cohort: 119 first-time mothers who had undergone kidney transplantation, compared to 238 first-time mothers who had not undergone transplantation, in Norway between 1969 and 2013
finding: This study shows that women who have undergone kidney transplantation have significantly higher rates of preeclampsia (particularly early-onset), cesarean delivery, preterm delivery, and delivering babies with a birth weight below the 10th centile compared to women who have not undergone transplantation.
mod_finding: This study found that kidney-transplanted women had significantly increased risks of preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, and preterm delivery compared to nontransplanted women.
